newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP wants assessment of EU research projects.
newsitem.headline: EP wants assessment of EU research projects.

text.p: The European Commission needs to come up with a convincing assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of European Union research activities, the European Parliament said on Thursday.
The Commission's first annual research and development report, for 1995, is good in parts but fails to live up to expectations, MEPs said in a report drafted by German Socialist Bernd Lange.

The Commission's report - COM(95)443 - provides a good summary of EU R&D activities but does not contain enough analysis of the facts it supplies. Nor does it provide adequate justification for the new priorities the Commission is proposing for research spending, MEPs said.
Lange's report also criticises the Commission for making only scant reference to the problems facing applicants for EU research funds.

These include the lack of clarity in certain calls for proposals; the frequently overcomplicated application procedure; and the need for applicants to use costly consultants to have any chance of getting accepted.
Parliament urged the Commission to improve its system of evaluating research activities in future.

"Without a convincing assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of research activities, it does not seem very responsible to support new projects and the release of new funding," Lange's report concludes.
